summary: Sourced defect account for the opt-in RestoreCommittedLogs startup replay: NewRaft feeds the FSM by a blocking send on the 128-slot fsmMutateCh (api.go 560, raft.go 1306) in batches of MaxAppendEntries before the only consumer, runFSM, is started (api.go 606 vs 637; fsm.go 241), so a committed-but-unapplied replay window above 128*MaxAppendEntries (8192 at the default) can never be drained and NewRaft cannot return — with no internal repair, since the caller holds no *Raft to call Shutdown. Recorded sources, two knowledge entries, one active investigation, and a source-only interpretation (defect_claim asserted, conclusion conditional) that flags the opt-in scope and the untested exact boundary. Submitted a focused five-case probe (real single-voter node, real commit-tracking store, restart over unchanged stores) that varies only the replay window and MaxAppendEntries; it reports the persisted commit index, the prepareLog-rule entry census over the window, the batch estimate, the read-back channel capacity, the restart return/non-return, and the blocked goroutine stack, so the retained execution can confirm or defeat the mechanism. Verified locally with native feedback: windows 4001 and 1000 return in ~1ms, window 12001 (188 batches) and window 1001 with MaxAppendEntries=4 (250 batches) do not return, and the same 12000-entry state returns in 2ms once a snapshot before shutdown shrinks the window to 0; the blocked stack sits in processLogs -> restoreFromCommittedLogs -> NewRaft.
